One timed operation inside a trace, with a span id, parent and tags.
Thread-bound key-value context in logging (correlation id, trace id) added to every log line.
Health check saying the process is alive; failure makes the platform restart it.
Health check saying the instance can take traffic; failure removes it from rotation without restarting.
A reliability target such as 99.9 percent of requests under 500 ms over 30 days; the remainder is the error budget.
Latency, traffic, errors and saturation: the four core service health measurements.
Number of distinct values of a metric tag; high cardinality (user ids) explodes time series.
Marks a method as a message consumer handled by a Spring listener container.
An ordered log shard of a Kafka topic; ordering is guaranteed only within a partition.
A message position in a partition; consumers commit offsets to record progress.
Broker-agnostic messaging with functional Consumer, Function and Supplier beans bound to destinations by binders.
Reassignment of partitions when consumers join or leave a group; redelivers from the last committed offset.
Spring reactive, non-blocking web stack on Netty using an event loop.
The reactive library behind Spring WebFlux, providing Mono and Flux.
A Reactor publisher of zero or one item; lazy until subscribed.
A Reactor publisher of zero to many items; lazy until subscribed.
A small set of threads handling many connections via callbacks; must never be blocked.
Reactive Relational Database Connectivity: a non-blocking SQL driver API for reactive applications.
Tool that detects blocking calls on non-blocking threads, used in reactive tests.
Build-time processing that generates bean definition code and reflection hints for fast startup and native images.
Ahead-of-time compiled native executable: very fast start and low memory, with a closed-world restriction on reflection.
Micrometer abstraction (Spring 6) that instruments code once to produce metrics, traces and log context.
Automated refactoring tool with recipes for Spring Boot 3 migration (package renames, property changes).
Spring 6.1 fluent API over JdbcTemplate for SQL queries and updates.
Root interface of List, Set and Queue: a group of single elements. Map is a separate hierarchy.
Resizable-array List: O(1) index access, amortised O(1) append, O(n) insert or remove in the middle. The default List.
Doubly linked List and Deque: O(1) at the ends, O(n) by index, high per-node memory. Rarely the best choice.
HashSet that also remembers insertion order using a linked list through its entries.
Sorted Set backed by a red-black tree: O(log n) operations and range views (floor, ceiling, headSet).
Resizable circular-array Deque: the fastest stack and queue in Java; does not allow null elements.
Binary-heap queue whose head is the smallest (or comparator-first) element: offer and poll are O(log n), peek O(1); iteration is not sorted.
External ordering strategy (compare(a, b)); compose with comparing, thenComparing and reversed.
Iterator that throws ConcurrentModificationException when the collection is structurally changed during iteration, detected with modCount. Best effort only.
List iterator that can move backward, know its index, and add, set or remove while iterating.
A tree stored in an array where every parent is smaller (min-heap) or larger (max-heap) than its children, so the top element is always the smallest or largest.
more: Removing the top costs O(log n). It is what PriorityQueue uses. Not related to the JVM heap.

short: Average cost per operation over a long sequence, even though an occasional operation (such as an array resize) costs O(n).
Stable hybrid merge and insertion sort used by List.sort and Arrays.sort for objects; may reject inconsistent comparators.
Shorthand for a lambda that calls an existing method: Type::staticMethod, instance::method, Type::instanceMethod or Type::new.
Functional interface T to boolean (test); composes with and, or, negate.
Functional interface T to R (apply); composes with andThen and compose.
Functional interface T to void (accept): performs an action on a value.
Functional interface () to T (get): produces or lazily creates a value.
A local variable never reassigned after initialisation; the only locals a lambda or inner class may capture.
A function together with the variables it captured from its enclosing scope; Java lambdas close over effectively final locals.
A function whose result depends only on its arguments and which has no side effects; safe to reorder, repeat or run in parallel.
Lazy, single-use pipeline of operations over a source; it stores no data and does not modify the source.
A lazy stream step such as filter, map or sorted that returns a new stream.
A stream step such as collect, count or reduce that runs the pipeline and consumes the stream.
Work is deferred until needed: stream intermediate operations run only when a terminal operation starts the pipeline.
A stream operation that can finish without consuming all elements: limit, findFirst, anyMatch, takeWhile.
Mutable reduction that gathers stream elements into a list, map, summary or string: toList, groupingBy, partitioningBy, joining.
Maps each element to a stream (or Optional) and flattens the results into one; use it for one-to-many and nested structures.
Folds stream elements into one value with an associative function and an identity.
Stream processed by several threads of the common ForkJoinPool; helps only for large, CPU-bound, stateless work.
Traversal and partitioning counterpart of Iterator that lets streams split a source for parallel processing.
Thread-safe list that copies its array on every write; readers never lock and iterate a snapshot. Best for read-mostly data.
Sorted, navigable concurrent map and set based on a skip list; the concurrent counterpart of TreeMap.
Probabilistic layered linked list giving O(log n) search; allows lock-free concurrent updates.
Iterator of a concurrent collection: never throws ConcurrentModificationException and may or may not reflect later changes.
Special sentinel item put on a queue to tell consumers to stop.
Algorithm in which some thread always makes progress without holding a lock, typically using CAS retry loops.
An isolated process started from an image, limited by cgroups and separated by namespaces; it shares the host kernel.
Immutable, layered, content-addressed package of an app and its file system, referenced by tag or digest.
Text recipe of instructions (FROM, COPY, RUN, ENTRYPOINT) that builds an image, one cached layer per instruction.
A read-only file-system diff in an image; layers are cached and shared between images.
Dockerfile with several FROM stages: build with the full toolchain, then copy only the artefact into a small runtime image.
Kernel feature giving a process its own view of PIDs, network, mounts, hostname and users; the basis of container isolation.
Kernel feature that limits and measures CPU, memory and I/O for a group of processes.
Open standards for container image format and runtime, so images run on Docker, containerd, CRI-O and others.
Docker-managed storage outside the container file system that survives container removal.
Maps a host directory into a container; handy for development, tied to the host layout.
Tool and YAML format that defines and runs a multi-container application with one command.
Dockerfile instruction for the process a container runs; use the exec (JSON array) form so the process is PID 1 and receives signals.
The first process in a container; it receives SIGTERM on stop and must handle it, or the container is killed after the grace period.
Container killed by the kernel for exceeding its memory limit (exit code 137); a JVM needs headroom above its heap.
JVM flag that sizes the maximum heap as a percentage of the container memory limit.
Minimal runtime images with no shell or package manager, giving a smaller attack surface.
Google tool that builds optimised, layered container images for Java apps without a Docker daemon.
Build images from source without a Dockerfile; Spring Boot offers spring-boot:build-image.
Container orchestrator that schedules containers across machines and reconciles actual state with the declared desired state.
Smallest Kubernetes unit: one or more containers sharing a network namespace and volumes, scheduled together; ephemeral.
Kubernetes controller that keeps a given number of identical pods running.
Kubernetes object that manages ReplicaSets to give declarative rolling updates and rollbacks for stateless apps.
Kubernetes workload with stable pod names, stable storage and ordered start; for databases and brokers.
Runs one pod on every node (log shippers, monitoring agents).
Stable virtual IP and DNS name that load-balances across the ready pods matching a label selector.
Kubernetes object plus controller routing external HTTP(S) to Services by host and path and terminating TLS.
Kubernetes object holding non-sensitive configuration injected as environment variables or files.
Object for sensitive data; only base64-encoded by default, so restrict with RBAC and encrypt etcd or use an external manager.
Node agent that starts the containers of its pods, runs probes and reports status to the API server.
Distributed key-value store holding all Kubernetes cluster state.
Kubernetes control-plane front door: every kubectl call and component goes through it.
A controller repeatedly compares desired state with observed state and acts to close the gap; the source of self-healing.
Kubernetes check that delays liveness and readiness until a slow-starting app has started.
Requests are the capacity the scheduler reserves; limits are the ceiling: CPU is throttled above it, memory above it is OOMKilled.
Scales the replica count of a Deployment based on CPU, memory or custom metrics.
Limits how many pods of an app may be voluntarily taken down at once, e.g. during node drains.
Replacing pods gradually, controlled by maxSurge and maxUnavailable, so the service stays available.
Pod state where a container keeps crashing and Kubernetes restarts it with growing delays; check logs --previous and events.
Kubernetes rule limiting which pods may talk to which; the default is allow all.
A pod's request for storage, bound to a PersistentVolume that a StorageClass provisions.
Package manager for Kubernetes: templated manifests (charts) with values per environment.
Sending a small share of traffic to the new version before rolling it out to everyone.
Two full environments; traffic is switched from the old (blue) to the new (green) at once, allowing instant rollback.
Mutable, non-thread-safe character buffer for building text efficiently; the default for concatenation in loops.
Legacy thread-safe StringBuilder with synchronized methods; rarely needed.
An object whose state cannot change after construction: thread-safe, safe as a map key, easy to reason about.
Concise final class whose components are private final fields, with generated accessors, constructor, equals, hashCode and toString.
Java 9 optimisation: a String stores Latin-1 text in one byte per character and falls back to UTF-16.
Two UTF-16 chars that together encode one Unicode code point outside the basic plane, such as most emoji.
A Unicode character number; may need one or two Java chars. Use codePoints() and codePointCount() to count correctly.
Mapping between characters and bytes (UTF-8, ISO-8859-1); always specify it explicitly, for example StandardCharsets.UTF_8.
Compiler evaluates constant expressions such as "a" + "b" at compile time, so the result is a pooled literal.
Placeholder such as T in a generic declaration, replaced by a concrete type by the caller.
Restriction on a type parameter, e.g. T extends Comparable<T>, so the code may call that type's methods.
The ? in generic types: ? extends T (read-only producer), ? super T (write-only consumer) or ? (unknown).
Rule for wildcards: use extends for a parameter you read from and super for one you write to.
Generic types are invariant: List<Integer> is not a List<Number>, which keeps collections type-safe.
A subtype can be used where its supertype is expected: arrays are covariant (unsafe), and ? extends T gives read-only covariance for generics.
A generic class used without type arguments (List); disables compile-time checks and exists only for legacy code.
A variable of a parameterised type refers to an object of the wrong type, causing a surprising ClassCastException later.
A Class<T> argument (or a TypeReference subclass) that carries a type to run time, working around erasure.
Annotation asserting a generic varargs method does not misuse its array, suppressing heap-pollution warnings.
Compiler warning that a generic operation (raw type, cast) cannot be verified and may cause heap pollution.
Caching pattern where each write goes to the cache and the database together, keeping reads fresh at the cost of slower writes.
Caching pattern where writes go to the cache and are flushed to the database later in batches; fast, but data can be lost if the cache fails first.
Caching pattern where the cache layer itself loads missing data from the database, so the caller only talks to the cache.
Reloading a hot cache entry in the background before its TTL ends, so readers never see a miss.
Removal of still-valid cache entries when memory is full, chosen by a policy such as LRU or LFU; different from TTL expiry.
Redis setting that caps memory use; when reached, the maxmemory-policy decides whether to evict keys or reject writes.
Eviction policy that removes the entry used least often, protecting consistently hot keys from one-off scans.
Cache hits divided by hits plus misses; the main measure of whether a cache is worth having.
Many cache keys expiring together, or the cache restarting empty, so the database receives the full load at once; reduced by TTL jitter and warm-up.
Repeated requests for keys that do not exist, which always miss the cache and hit the database; countered by null markers and Bloom filters.
Compact probabilistic set that says an item is definitely absent or possibly present: no false negatives, a small rate of false positives.
A single key receiving so much traffic that it overloads one cache node; mitigated with a local cache or key copies.
An oversized Redis value or collection that blocks the single command thread when read or deleted; split it and use UNLINK.
Redis component that monitors a primary, promotes a replica when it fails and tells clients the new address.
Redis sharding mode that splits keys over 16,384 hash slots across several primaries, each with replicas.
One of 16,384 buckets in Redis Cluster; a key's slot is CRC16(key) mod 16384 and each slot belongs to one primary.
Part of a Redis key in braces, such as {user42}:cart, that alone is hashed so related keys land in the same cluster slot.
Redis persistence option that writes periodic point-in-time dumps; compact and quick to load but can lose recent writes.
Redis persistence option that logs every write and replays it on restart; more durable than RDB, with a larger file.
Sending many commands without waiting for each reply to save network round trips; not atomic.
Script run atomically inside Redis, used for check-and-set logic such as releasing a lock only if you own it.
Redis command that iterates the key space in small cursor-based steps without blocking, unlike KEYS.
Algorithm for a distributed lock across several independent Redis nodes; debated because process pauses can still break safety without fencing.
Default Redis client in Spring Boot: non-blocking, with thread-safe connections shared between threads.
Java Redis client that adds distributed locks, semaphores, rate limiters and collections on top of Redis.
Letting only one request rebuild a missing value while concurrent callers wait for its result, preventing a stampede.
Umbrella Spring project giving one repository programming model over many stores (JPA, JDBC, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, R2DBC).
Spring project for bulk jobs: chunked read-process-write with a transaction per chunk, restart, skip and retry, and job history.
Spring project implementing enterprise integration patterns (channels, routers, transformers) for message-driven integration.
Spring project that stores HTTP sessions externally (Redis, JDBC) so they survive instance restarts and scaling.
Spring project for enforcing and testing module boundaries inside a monolith, easing a later split into services.
Web tool and API that generates a Spring Boot project with chosen dependencies.
Spring helper over JDBC that removes connection, statement and exception boilerplate while you still write SQL.
Default JDBC connection pool in Spring Boot: fast, small, reuses database connections.
Spring test support that loads and caches an ApplicationContext across test classes.
Red Hat's enterprise Kubernetes distribution: Kubernetes plus secure defaults, builds, registry, router, console and Operators.
The community, open source upstream of OpenShift.
OpenShift policy that controls what a pod may do (user ID, capabilities, privileged mode, host access); the default restricted-v2 forbids root.
OpenShift build strategy that injects source code into a builder image to produce an application image without a Dockerfile.
OpenShift resource tracking image tags and digests, so the cluster can trigger builds or rollouts when an image changes.
OpenShift resource describing how to build an image: source, strategy (S2I, Docker, pipeline) and output.
OpenShift resource that publishes a Service on a hostname through the router, with TLS termination and weighted backends.
OpenShift and Kubernetes component that installs, updates and manages Operators from catalogues.
Catalogue of Operators (Red Hat, certified partners, community) installable from the OpenShift console.
Controller that manages an application through a custom resource, automating install, scaling, backup and upgrade.
Kubernetes-native CI framework where Tasks and Pipelines are custom resources and each step runs in a pod.
GitOps controller that continuously syncs a cluster to manifests in Git and reports drift.
Operating model where Git holds the desired state of the system and an automated agent applies and reconciles it.
Immutable, container-optimised operating system used for OpenShift nodes and managed by the cluster.
Lightweight container runtime for Kubernetes used by OpenShift, implementing the Container Runtime Interface.

A label on a Compose service so it starts only when you ask for it: docker compose --profile debug up.

Command Docker runs periodically to decide whether a container is healthy; Compose can wait for it with service_healthy.
Tool that runs a Kubernetes cluster with each node as a Docker container; fast and used for CI and testing.
Default network plugin (CNI) of kind clusters.
Tool that runs a local single or multi-node Kubernetes cluster through a driver, with an addon catalogue.
